text.p: Precious metals closed higher overnight, helped by some year-end short covering and stronger than expected U.S. November housing starts.
Copper closed well above support levels after a more bullish than expected stocks report but oil and wheat prices eased.
The CRB index was down 1.05 at 244.53.

LME copper whipsawed on Tuesday after a more bullish than expected stocks report shook up the market as it approached the slow holiday period. "That (stock data) caught the market by surprise. It showed the market was tighter than we thought," one senior floor trader said. LME inventories increased by only 2,875 tonnes after some traders expected a rise of up to 12,000 tonnes.

Prices burst back above $2,100 resistance as traders rushed to cover shorts in the morning, hovered there in a narrow range in the afternoon, but slipped backed below $2,100 in late floor trading. Three month copper finished the afternoon kerb at $2,095, up $14 and well above key $2,080 support.
It traded in a range of $2,077 to $2,118.

Many players had expected prices to drift to the $2,000 level or below in the traditionally slow period surrounding the western Christmas holidays after tight December dates had passed and the cash premium eased.
The cash/threes backwardation edged down $5 to $50.

"Now we could very well see prices hold above $2,000 and more tightness emerge in the New Year," another floor trader said, adding that some positions had been rolled over to February and March. But traders were wary and broker Rudolf Wolff said in a commentary any confirmed breach of the $2,080 level would target $2,000 based on a head and shoulders pattern.
Any move above $2,100 would find resistance at $2,150.

Nickel consolidated after crumbling to fresh 26-month lows on Monday under the weight of speculative selling and weak fundamentals. It ended at $6,575, up $65, but chartists said the damaged technical picture targeted falls to $6,400 in coming weeks.

Tin bounced from Monday's new 19-month lows, finishing the afternoon kerb at $5,830, up $145. Analysts said the recovery from oversold levels may be temporary and if the market fails to build a base further weakness could take prices to $5,600 or $5,500.
Aluminium continued its independent path, gradually climbing higher amid the gyrations of the others.
Trade buying and forward orders in the physical market continue to buoy prices, analysts say.
Traders said a round of late short-covering on the kerb helped three month prices finish at $1,530, up $14.
Zinc ended up $10 at $1,055, a near-term resistance level, and lead finished the day firmer at $701 versus $689/90 on Monday.
New York precious metals futures ended higher Tuesday, helped by some year-end fund short covering, against the background of higher-than-expected US November housing starts, traders said.

"Silver looks like it might have more upside potential, but overall today's action was probably just a blip up caused by fund short covering and the big housing starts number," Linnco Futures Group's Chicago trader Anthony Raia said.

U.S. November housing starts were 1.415 million at an annual rate, up 9.2 percent, the biggest monthly rise since July 1995. But the U.S. Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged, as expected, seeing little evidence of inflation.
COMEX February gold closed up 60 cents at $370.50 an ounce, but failed to clear resistance around $372.00.
Estimated gold futures volume was 37,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $368.40/368.80, up from the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $368.20, and the New York close Monday at $367.80/368.30.
Further weakness in U.S. bond and stock markets early Tuesday also helped provide some support.
Precious metals have been consolidating in the past 10 days after spot gold slid to a three year low at $366.00 an ounce at the end of November.
"Interim support remains at $367 an ounce in February gold, with a major technical target of $364 on the downside," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.

"A sell off to those levels cannot be ruled out in the next week or two, but $364 appears to be a strong technical base and there has been evidence of some significant buying in Asia at prices below $370," he said.
"If the market holds around $370, prices could stage a modest rebound," he added.
January crude on NYMEX was off 24 cents at US$25.50 a barrel in late trading, following a fall in heating oil on talk that stocks were rising.

CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby December hit hard by the posting on Tuesday of 460,000 bushels for delivery on that contract. Wheat closed 9-1/4 cents per bushel lower to two cents higher, with December down 9-1/4 at US$4.04-1/2.
